body.x: Monit Corp (CEO and Co-Founder Tony Park) participated in CES 2024, which took place from January 9th (Tuesday) to January 12th (Friday) in Las Vegas, USA.

Monit started as a research project at Samsung C-Lab in 2016. After successfully validating its business model, it became an independent corporation through a spin-off with support from Samsung Venture Investment in April 2017. Founded by four engineers with a background from Samsung Electronics, the company oversees all development internally. Monit is known for its distinctive technological prowess, particularly in diaper detection systems that combine advanced detection algorithms based on IoT communication.

In this manner, Monit has successfully developed its proprietary diaper status monitoring system called ‘MECS (Monit Elderly Care System).’ Through this system, the company aims to address common issues such as urinary tract infections and pressure sores that often occur in elderly patients requiring care. Additionally, it anticipates improving the efficiency of diaper-related tasks for caregivers.

MECS monitors the diaper status in real-time and notifies when a change is needed. The primary goal is to minimize the risk of infections that can occur when diapers remain unchanged while also allowing for the management of diaper usage and bedding. The upcoming version of MECS for care facilities manages multiple patients simultaneously in settings such as hospitals and nursing homes. With the capability to monitor the diaper status of various patients concurrently, it enhances caregiver quality and reduces the complexity of management. Optimizing the ability to manage multiple patients simultaneously improves operational efficiency, and the system can meet the facility’s specific requirements.

In addition, Monit introduced an AI chatbot service for parenting beginners at the exhibition. This chatbot app provides trustworthy advice and information related to parenting in a question-and-answer format, offering refined data verified by experts to address queries about parenting promptly.

body.x: A Monit representative stated, “We are forming partnerships and collaborating closely with various companies to enter the European and Japanese markets. We particularly targeted Japan because the aging population issue in Japan is similar to that of South Korea, and there is a high preference for Korean companies in Japan. It is meaningful that many Japanese investment firms and companies visited our booth at CES 2024,” adding, “We also had meetings with representatives from the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP). Through participating in CES 2024, we aim to explore opportunities in the North American market and contribute our technology to address aging-related challenges worldwide, including the United States.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
